name: hex glinski flanks one way
description: Glinski-style hexagonal chess on a native 91-cell hexagon, with promotion on the far edge, whose two empty flanks are joined. The upper-left and lower-right sides, the two flanks no army stands on, are one seam that each player may cross one way only: the first player by leaving by the lower right and coming back in on the upper left, the second the reverse, which is the same rule turned half a turn. Every cell has six neighbours. A rook slides through the six edge neighbours, a bishop through the six cells that touch two of them, a queen does both, a king steps one cell in any of those twelve directions, and a knight leaps to the twelve nearest cells no rook or bishop line reaches. A pawn steps straight forward, two on its first move, and takes on the two neighbours either side of forward. A pawn that reaches the far edge, the eleven cells from which it has no step forward, becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight. There is no en passant and no castling. Each side has a king, a queen, two rooks, two knights, three bishops and nine pawns in a wedge. The second army is the first turned half a turn, so each king faces the other queen and each side promotes on the cells the other army started from. Checkmate wins; stalemate is a draw.
